name: Götzens
kurzbeschreibung: Sunny residential community on the Mittelgebirge with stunning views of the Stubaier Alpen and the Inntal.
beschreibung:
Overview

Götzens is located at an altitude of 868 metres on the sunny Western Plateau in the Tyrolean district of Innsbruck-Land, just eight kilometres southwest of the provincial capital Innsbruck. The charming village is home to approximately 4,150 residents and, together with neighbouring Birgitz, Axams, and Mutters, forms one of the most desirable residential and holiday regions around Innsbruck. The village is characterised by handsome Tyrolean farmhouses, historic architecture, and an active local community. Its prime setting unites the tranquillity of a rural alpine community with direct access to Innsbruck's urban cultural life and alpine sporting grounds. To the south, the forested mountains rise toward the Pfriemesköpfl and the striking 2,403-metre Nockspitze peak, while to the north, open views stretch across the Inn Valley toward the limestone walls of the Nordkette.

History

Götzens is among the oldest documented settlements on the plateau, first recorded around 1128 as Gecens in monastic chronicles of Tegernsee Abbey. During the Middle Ages, the fortified fortress of Vellenberg crowned a wooded hilltop within the municipality, serving as the seat of the Sonnenburg court; in 1427, the famed Tyrolean minnesinger and knight Oswald von Wolkenstein was imprisoned within its towers. Internationally renowned, Götzens is celebrated for its parish church of St. Peter and Paul, constructed between 1772 and 1775 by master builder Franz Singer. It is widely considered one of the finest Rococo village churches in the entire Alpine region. The interior features delicate stucco work by the local Singer school, sweeping ceiling frescoes by Bavarian master Matthäus Günther, and phenomenal acoustic qualities that host acclaimed classical concerts. The church also preserves the relics of the blessed martyr priest Otto Neururer.

Getting There

By car, travellers reach Götzens from Innsbruck within 10 to 15 minutes via the Inntal Autobahn A12, taking either the Innsbruck-Süd exit via Mutters or the Zirl-Ost/Kematen exit ascending the plateau. Rail passengers arrive at Innsbruck Central Station, a major international rail junction with direct ICE and Railjet connections across Europe. From Innsbruck station, regional VVT bus route 404 runs directly to Götzens every 15 to 30 minutes, continuing toward Axams. Alternatively, the romantic Stubaitalbahn light railway departs from Innsbruck to Mutters, connecting to a brief regional feeder bus to Götzens.

Tips

A prime attraction for outdoor enthusiasts is the Götzner Bahn, a modern 8-seater gondola on the edge of the village that whisks visitors up to the 1,800-metre Pfriemesköpfl and into the Muttereralm ski and hiking area. The challenging 4.5-kilometre Götzner downhill run served as the official Olympic reserve track for the women's downhill races. In summer, the mountain features mountain cart tracks, the Innsbruck Bikepark, and family walking trails leading to the Götzner Alm hut at 1,542 metres for traditional Tyrolean dumplings. Lovers of art should not miss visiting the Rococo parish church and attending one of its renowned sacred music concerts. Furthermore, the two-time Olympic ski resort of Axamer Lizum lies only a ten-minute drive away.
